summary.one_liner: A local-first router that sits under Claude Code (and other coding agents) and drafts each prompt's answer on a free or local model before Claude takes the turn, to conserve subscription quota.
summary.what_it_does: llm-router hooks into the coding tool's lifecycle and reads each prompt before the host model does. A free regex heuristic classifies the prompt, and routable prompts get a draft from a free or local model first, walking up toward paid models only when needed. Drafts are passed to Claude as advisory hints by default; an opt-in zero-Claude mode and a tool-call enforcement setting (LLM_ROUTER_ENFORCE) control this. It reports verified and unverified savings separately via status and savings-report commands, plus a session-end summary with tier mix, per-provider cost and latency percentiles. It also includes a secret-detection path that keeps prompts containing API keys or private keys on loopback Ollama models, a grounding check that discards drafts citing absent files, and optional direct execution of file and command tools under a confined path. It can also be used in-process from Python via a Router class with a budget cap.
use_cases: Stretch a Claude Pro or Max subscription by offloading simple questions
Route coding-agent prompts to free or local models first
Track estimated savings versus API list price
Keep secrets in prompts on local models only
Budget-capped LLM calls from Python code
Fall back automatically when a model provider fails or rate-limits
notable: Works with no API keys on a Claude Pro/Max subscription by routing through MCP tools and local models
Supports many hosts: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf and others via a single install command
Separates verified from unverified savings, each with its own sample size
Secret-bearing prompts are sent only to loopback Ollama models or refused
Circuit breakers skip failing or rate-limited providers
caveats: Routed answers are advisory by default; Claude still takes the turn unless zero-Claude mode is enabled
Direct execution of write/run tools is a static tripwire, not an OS sandbox, and does not stop targeted deletes or force pushes per the README
RouterArena benchmark results are self-graded and not yet independently verified
Team policy, audit export and SSO are offered by a separate sibling product, Chuzom, not this repo
Pi and Kimi Code hosts are planned but not yet supported
